You are a senior frontend engineer + product designer. Polish the main inbox UI of a hackathon product into something a stressed procurement buyer would actually use on a Sunday (demo Sunday 14:00; jury = Lio, judges "taste": one design language, clear layout, a clear recommendation and one click to act, right wording, no every-number-on-one-screen). Work directly in the repo; do NOT commit or push. Other engineers work in parallel: you may ONLY edit web/src/App.tsx, web/src/components/DecisionCard.tsx, web/src/components/Rail.tsx, web/src/components/StatusStrip.tsx, web/src/components/EvidenceDrawer.tsx, web/src/components/AlertsButton.tsx, web/src/lib/api.ts, web/src/index.css. Do NOT edit web/src/components/Routines.tsx or anything under web/src/components/routines/ (another engineer rebuilds them; keep App's usage `<Routines state={state} onChanged={load} request={automate} />` intact), SourceAnchors.tsx, VoiceCall.tsx, or any Python.

Repo: /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony. Stack: React 19, Tailwind v4 (tokens in web/src/index.css), lucide-react, radix Sheet (web/src/components/ui/sheet.tsx), Button (ui/button.tsx). No new npm packages. The app is served live from this checkout at http://127.0.0.1:8000 (login form /login; password = ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env, never print it). The UI was written by a teammate (Akshat) and extended by us; keep his structure, improve it.

Expert findings to fix (verify each in the code and in screenshots first):
1. ONE automation offer. Today there are two competing ones: a bottom toast in App.tsx (`AutomateOffer`, appears after any card goes from open to decided, by button or voice) and a hard-coded block in DecisionCard.tsx (~lines 200-212: "Send routine ETA chasers like this one automatically… Allow always / Ask me each time", driven by offer_trust from the approve response). Replace both with one inline panel pinned at the top of the right column (above "Needs you"), rounded-xl border-2 border-ok/40 bg-ok/5 p-4: "Approved: <headline>" (use Sent/Escalated/Dismissed accordingly) / "Handle the next one like this on its own?" / "You'll see what it would do before it starts. Anything that costs money or changes the plan still comes to you." Buttons "Show me how" (sets `automate` state → Routines sheet opens and drafts) and "Not now". On the single decision page (/d/<id>) show the same panel under the card. Keep the open→decided detection in App.load (it also catches voice decisions). Remove the trust offer UI and the onOffer/offer plumbing if it becomes dead (keep /api/trust untouched server-side).
2. Activity / history: items handled by a routine should show a chip "By routine · <name>" (lucide Workflow icon, text-xs font-semibold text-ok bg-ok/10 rounded px-1.5). The backend is being extended in parallel to add `via?: string` (e.g. "routine: Tell DC site lead to collect at port", or "voice", "inbox") to activity items in /api/state; add `via?: string` to the ActivityItem type and render the chip when it starts with "routine:" (also a small Mic chip "By voice" for "voice"). Make it robust when the field is missing.
3. Header/status strip contradictions: Collector's shows "On track" with "-7 h slack" (show slack only when meaningful: if on track and slack is negative or there is nothing at risk, show "–" or omit it); "Breaks first CMP-GAM-001" shows a raw part code — show a readable name if available in state (check the strip item and cards for a part name; otherwise hide the code); "Last portal drop 8 h ago" looks dead → "Watching the portal · checked <ago>" using last_check_at. Keep numbers consistent with cards where possible; do not invent numbers.
4. Wording/consistency: one cost wording "No cost" (cards show "none" in places), status words capitalised ("Approved", not "approved"), section headings one style (text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-ink-3), no emoji in UI text, no internal codes (amber/level/routine_type/channel) anywhere visible.
5. Decision card: make the primary action unmistakable (Approve as the one primary button; Edit, Escalate, Dismiss secondary; consider a "⋯" for Dismiss), keep "Talk it through", Evidence, Agent trail. The recommended option block should read like a recommendation with its effect/cost. Make the "system says vs document says" visible on the card itself in one compact line if the card has such evidence (e.g. "SAP: 48,000 due Sat · Document: 20,000 arrive Tue"), linking to Evidence.
6. Mobile (390 px wide): status strip must not overflow; header buttons must not wrap under it; cards readable. Desktop 1440 px must stay clean.
7. Anything else that makes it feel like one product (spacing rhythm, alignment, empty states e.g. "Nothing needs you right now" with what the agents are watching).

Verify: `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npm run build` must pass. Check visually with headless Chrome screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 (e.g. `PW=... uv run --quiet --with playwright python script.py` with `p.chromium.launch(channel="chrome")`, log in via the /login form; scripts and screenshots in /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/ui-inbox/). NEVER click Approve/Escalate/Dismiss on real cards in your checks (approving sends real supplier emails); to see the decided/offer states, temporarily mock in the browser (e.g. intercept /api/state with page.route) instead of changing server data. Final report: what changed per file, screenshot paths, and anything the lead must wire in the backend.

"""
Screenshot the inbox at desktop and phone width. Never clicks decision buttons.

Usage: PW=... python shot.py <prefix> [mock]
mock: none | decided (latest open card flips to approved on the 2nd poll) | calm | via
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.request
import base64

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
prefix = sys.argv[1]
mock = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "none"
pw = os.environ["PW"]

req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/api/state")
req.add_header("Authorization", "Basic " + base64.b64encode(f"x:{pw}".encode()).decode())
real = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))


def variant(n: int) -> dict:
    s = json.loads(json.dumps(real))
    if mock == "calm":
        for c in s["cards"]:
            c["status"] = "approved"
    if mock in ("decided", "via") and n > 1:
        c = next(c for c in s["cards"] if c["status"] == "open" and not c["routed_to_other"])
        c["status"] = "sent"
        s["activity"].insert(0, {"at": s["now"], "kind": "approved", "card": c["id"], "text": f"Sent: {c['headline']}", "via": "inbox"})
    if mock == "via":
        s["activity"][1:1] = [
            {"at": s["now"], "kind": "approved", "text": "Sent: Collect clear cases from the port", "via": "routine: Tell DC site lead to collect at port"},
            {"at": s["now"], "kind": "escalated", "text": "Escalated: allocate game cards", "via": "voice"},
        ]
    return s


with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch(channel="chrome")
    for name, vp in (("desk", {"width": 1440, "height": 900}), ("phone", {"width": 390, "height": 844})):
        ctx = b.new_context(viewport=vp, device_scale_factor=1 if name == "desk" else 2)
        page = ctx.new_page()
        page.goto(BASE + "/login")
        page.fill("input[name=password]", pw)
        page.click("button")
        page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
        calls = {"n": 0}

        def handle(route):
            calls["n"] += 1
            route.fulfill(status=200, content_type="application/json", body=json.dumps(variant(calls["n"])))

        if mock != "none":
            page.route("**/api/state", handle)
        path = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "/"
        page.goto(BASE + path)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1500 if mock == "none" else 6500)
        page.screenshot(path=f"{OUT}/{prefix}-{name}.png", full_page=name == "phone")
        ctx.close()
    b.close()
print("ok")

content.text:
I've polished the inbox in the seven files you allowed, and nothing is committed. Typecheck and `npm run build` both pass; the bare `tsc -p .` checks nothing here because `tsconfig.json` has `files: []`, so I ran `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`.

**Heads-up:** the app serves `web/dist` directly, so every build I ran went straight to the live app at :8000.

I never clicked Approve, Escalate or Dismiss on a real card. The decided, routine/voice and empty states were faked by intercepting `/api/state` in the browser.

**What changed, per file**
- **`lib/api.ts`**: added the optional `via` field to activity items, plus shared helpers:
  - turn part codes like `CMP-GAM-001` into readable names from the cards, or hide them;
  - strip bracketed internal codes and show ISO dates as "Mon 23 Nov";
  - one cost wording, so "none" becomes "No cost";
  - slack text that hides itself when it would only confuse.
- **`App.tsx`**:
  - The bottom toast and the `offer` plumbing are gone; open→decided detection stays in `load`, so voice decisions still count.
  - The offer is skipped when a routine made the decision or one already exists for that card.
  - "Show me how" sets `automate`, which opens the Routines sheet and starts a draft.
  - On `/d/<id>`, the same panel shows under the card, with a Routines button in that header so the sheet can open there. The main `<Routines state={state} onChanged={load} request={automate} />` is unchanged.
- **`Rail.tsx`**: holds the one automation panel, pinned above "Needs you", with your wording and Sent/Approved/Escalated/Dismissed as appropriate.
  - All section headings now use one style.
  - Activity items get a "By routine · <name>" chip or a "By voice" chip, and show nothing extra when `via` is missing.
  - The empty state now reads "Nothing needs you right now." with what the agents are watching (shipments, suppliers, last check). It no longer says "On track" while the header says the line stops.
- **`DecisionCard.tsx`**:
  - Approve is the one primary button, full width on phones; Edit and Escalate are secondary, and Dismiss moved into a "⋯" menu.
  - The recommendation reads "We recommend", then the action, the effect and a cost tag. Alternatives read "Or: …" with their cost.
  - Cards with a system-vs-document mismatch show both sides on the card ("SYSTEM · SAP purchase order: 48,000 due Sat 21 Nov" vs "DOCUMENT: 28,000 flown · 20,000 arrive Tue 24 Nov"). Clicking it opens Evidence.
  - Decided cards show an "Approved" or "Sent" banner instead of the buttons.
  - The old hard-coded "Allow always / Ask me each time" block is gone. `/api/trust` is no longer called from the UI but still exists on the server.
- **`StatusStrip.tsx`**:
  - Collector's slack now shows "–" instead of "-7 h" when on track; Standard shows "−18 min".
  - "Breaks first" shows "Game Card 128 GB" instead of the part code, and clicking it scrolls to its card.
  - "Last portal drop 8 h ago" became "Watching · checked <ago>" under the logo.
  - On phones, the logo and header buttons share the top row, the two editions sit side by side below, and nothing overflows.
- **`EvidenceDrawer.tsx`**: generic "Evidence" titles became "Supporting note", and dates in the system/document values are tidied.

**Screenshots** (in `/Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/ui-inbox/`)
- Before: `before-desk.png`, `before-phone.png`
- After: `final-desk.png`, `final-phone.png`
- Offer panel: `decided-desk.png`, `decided-phone.png`
- Single decision page with the offer: `single-phone.png`
- Activity chips: `via-desk-bottom.png`, `via-phone-bottom.png`
- Empty state: `calm-phone.png`

The script is `shot.py` in the same folder.

**For you to wire in the backend**
- **`via` field:** activity items need `via` set to `"routine: <name>"`, `"voice"` or `"inbox"`. Until then, no chips show and routine decisions aren't filtered out of the offer.
- **Numbers that disagree:** the Standard strip says 32,000 at risk while the cards say 20,000 and 34,800. I didn't reconcile them in the UI because that would mean inventing a number.
- **Long option text:** some option text from the backend is long and phrased like an internal label ("Message approver of exceptions: Decision needed: …"). It needs shorter phrasing at the source.
- **Code names in names:** the part-name lookup relies on the cards (card ids ending in the code, or "(CODE)" in an option's text). A `part_name` field on the strip's `breaks_first` and on each card would be sturdier.

The working tree also has other people's uncommitted changes (Python files, `Routines.tsx`, `routines/`, `VoiceCall.tsx`); I didn't touch them.
